translationRepairs: Fa Xiong, styled Wenqiang, was a native of Mei in Fufeng and traced his line to Fa Zhang, son of King Xiang of Qi.
Fa Xiong, styled Wenqiang, was a native of Mei in Fufeng and traced his line to Fa Zhang, King Xiang of Qi.
齊襄王法章 is one person: Fa Zhang, King Xiang of Qi. It does not say that Fa Zhang was the king's son.
Fa Xiong, courtesy name Wenqiang, was a man of Mei in Fufeng, a descendant of King Xiang of Qi's son Fa Zhang.
Fa Xiong, courtesy name Wenqiang, was a man of Mei in Fufeng, a descendant of Fa Zhang, King Xiang of Qi.
The literal field makes the same false father-son division within the single title-and-name phrase 齊襄王法章.
He died in office in the early Yuanhe era (114–119 CE).
He died in office in the Yuanchu era (114–120 CE).
元初 is the Eastern Han Yuanchu era, AD 114-120; Yuanhe is written 元和 and belongs to a different reign period.
In the early Yuanhe period, he died in office.
During the Yuanchu era, he died in office.
元初中 means during the Yuanchu era; 中 need not restrict the death to the era's middle years. The old text names the wrong era.

The court cast about for commanders; the Three Excellencies nominated Teng Fu for his civil and military gifts. He received the post of commandant of Jiujiang and, with General of the Household Zhao Xu under Feng Gun, led tens of thousands of provincial troops against the rebels.

The court cast about for commanders; the Three Excellencies nominated Teng Fu for his civil and military gifts. He received the post of commandant of Jiujiang and, with General of the Household Zhao Xu, assisted Feng Gun in combining tens of thousands of provincial troops against the rebels.
與中郎將趙序助馮緄 coordinates Teng Fu and Zhao Xu as jointly assisting Feng Gun; it does not subordinate Zhao Xu alone.

Thereupon Gun was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, leading more than a hundred thousand troops to attack them. The edict enfeoffing Gun said: "The Man and Yi vex the Hua, long unrestful and unchastised; each has burned the capital city, trampled and trampled the officials.

Thereupon Gun was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, leading more than a hundred thousand troops to attack them. The edict enfeoffing Gun said: "The Man and Yi vex the Hua, long unrestful and unchastised; each has burned the capital city and trampled the officials.
The duplicated 'trampled' is an English artifact; 蹈籍 is a single verb phrase.

In the fifth year of Yanxi, Changsha and Lingling bandits joined to seven or eight thousand men, called themselves "General," entered Guiyang, Cangwu, Nanhai, and Jiaozhi; the governor of Jiaozhi and the grand administrator of Cangwu fled at the wind; two commanderies were both lost.

In the fifth year of Yanxi, Changsha and Lingling bandits joined forces, seven or eight thousand strong, styled themselves "General," and entered Guiyang, Cangwu, Nanhai, and Jiaozhi; the inspector of Jiaozhi and the grand administrator of Cangwu fled at the first rumor, and both commanderies were lost.
The proposal preserves the events while replacing the calque 望風, 'fled at the wind,' with natural English and correctly renders 刺史 as inspector.
What we lost today is trifling—don't dwell on it!"
What was lost is trifling—don't dwell on it!"
所亡少少 says only that the loss was slight; it contains no word meaning 'today.'
Inspector Du Shang, afraid I would speak first, panicked and memorialized that I had slandered him.
Inspector Du Shang, fearing I would report first and alarmed at his own culpability, submitted a secret memorial falsely accusing me.
The first-person 見誣 makes Zhang Pan the person falsely accused. The old translation reverses the accusation; the revision states its direction directly.

His elder brother Qiao was secretariat director; countenance and bearing were great and beautiful; repeatedly submitted speech on government affairs; Emperor Huan loved his talent and appearance; edict married him to a princess; Qiao firmly declined and was not listened to; thereupon closed mouth and did not eat, died in seven days.

His elder brother Qiao was a Master of Writing; countenance and bearing were great and beautiful; repeatedly submitted speech on government affairs; Emperor Huan loved his talent and appearance; an edict would marry him to a princess; Qiao firmly declined and was not listened to; thereupon he closed his mouth and did not eat, and died in seven days.
尚書 is Master of Writing, not the higher office 尚書令, Secretariat Director.
Xuan was able to use stratagem; also called shaking the troops.
Xuan was able to use stratagem; he is also said to have withdrawn the troops in good order.
振旅 is the orderly withdrawal or return of an army after a campaign, not literally 'shaking the troops.'
